questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Floor Function
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $⌊x⌋$ equals the greatest integer that is smaller than or equal to $x:$

$$
⌊x⌋=n,\,\text{where}\,n\le x<n+1,\,n\in Z.
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=0.5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.5) & =⌊3(0.5)+2⌋+2 \\  & =⌊1.5+2⌋+2 \\  & =⌊3.5⌋+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⌊3.5⌋=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.5) & =⌊3.5⌋+2 \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the value of $f(x)=\frac{{e}^{⌊1-x⌋}}{x}$ at $x=-1.5.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $⌊x⌋$ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x:$

$$
⌊x⌋=n,\,\text{where}\,n\le x<n+1,\,n\in Z.
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=-1.5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.5) & =\frac{{e}^{⌊1-(-1.5)⌋}}{(-1.5)} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{⌊1+1.5⌋}}{1.5} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{⌊2.5⌋}}{1.5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
⌊2.5⌋=2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.5) & =-\frac{{e}^{⌊2.5⌋}}{1.5} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2}}{1.5} \\  & =-4.926\,03… \\  & ≈-4.93,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem: Find the value of $f(x)=\frac{{3}^{⌈5x-2⌉}}{x}$ at $x=0.7.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $⌈x⌉$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x:$ 

$$
⌈x⌉=n,\,\text{where}\,n-1<x\le n,\,n\in Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=0.7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.7) & =\frac{{3}^{⌈5(0.7)-2⌉}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{⌈3.5-2⌉}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{⌈1.5⌉}}{0.7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
⌈1.5⌉=2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.7) & =\frac{{3}^{⌈1.5⌉}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{0.7} \\  & =\frac{9}{0.7} \\  & =12.857\,14… \\  & ≈12.86,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

canonical_examples.problem: If $f(x)=2x+\left\lfloor \dfrac{x}{5} \right\rfloor,$ then what is the value of $f(-0.5)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $\lfloor x \rfloor$ equals the greatest integer that is smaller than or equal to $x{:}$

$$
\lfloor x \rfloor = n,
\quad\text{where}\quad
n \leq x \lt n+1,\quad  n\in \mathbb Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=-0.5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-0.5) & =2\cdot (-0.5)+⌊\frac{-0.5}{5}⌋ \\  & =-1+⌊-0.1⌋.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⌊-0.1⌋=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-0.5) & =-1+⌊-0.1⌋ \\  & =-1+(-1) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the value of $f(x) = \dfrac{e^{\left\lfloor x+2 \right\rfloor}}{2x+1}$ at $x = 0.75.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $\lfloor x \rfloor$ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x{:}$

$$
\lfloor x \rfloor = n,
\quad\text{where}\quad
n \leq x \lt n+1,\quad  n\in \mathbb Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x = 0.75,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.75) & =\frac{{e}^{⌊0.75+2⌋}}{2(0.75)+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{⌊2.75⌋}}{2.5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
\left\lfloor 2.75\right\rfloor = 2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.75) & =\frac{{e}^{⌊2.75⌋}}{2.5} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{2.5} \\  & =2.955\,62… \\  & ≈2.96,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $\lceil x \rceil$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x{:}$ 

$$
\lceil x \rceil = n,
\quad\text{where}\quad
n-1 \lt x \leq n, \quad n\in\mathbb Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=0.4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.4) & =(⌈6(0.4)-3⌉-2)^{3} \\  & =(⌈2.4-3⌉-2)^{3} \\  & =(⌈-0.6⌉-2)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
\lceil -0.6 \rceil = 0.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.4) & =(⌈-0.6⌉-2)^{3} \\  & =(0-2)^{3} \\  & =(-2)^{3} \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the value of $f(x) = \left \lceil e^{6x-5} \right \rceil$ at $x = 1.25.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $\lceil x \rceil$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x{:}$ 

$$
\lceil x \rceil = n,
\quad\text{where}\quad
n-1 \lt x \leq n, \quad n\in\mathbb Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x = 1.25,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.25) & =⌈{e}^{6(1.25)-5}⌉ \\  & =⌈{e}^{7.5-5}⌉ \\  & =⌈{e}^{2.5}⌉.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$

$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.25) & =⌈{e}^{2.5}⌉ \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$
